extracted.intended_audience: advanced mathematics students and researchers in category theory and related areas (algebra/topology)
extracted.subtask_description: Expository textbook material giving precise definitions, hypotheses, and proof-sketches for Beck's theorem (tripleability/monadicity), examples (varieties, compact Hausdorff spaces), and the axioms and coherence theorem for monoidal categories. Useful as a reference for when a functor is monadic and for monoidal-category coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fork condition for T-algebra (split fork (4))
rubrics_metrics.description: The maps of a T-algebra correspond to being a fork in X split by T: the fork condition h ° Jl.x = h ° Th (for (4)) is the associative law for h; h ° t'lx is 1 because of the unit law for (x,h); additional equations follow from the unit law for T and naturality of t'l.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies algebra axioms (associativity and unit) with a split-fork diagram; use this correspondence when relating algebra structures to coequalizer/fork diagrams (basis for the comparison/construction arguments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical presentation of an object a (fork (5))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each object a in A, the adjunction (F,G,e,t'l): X ⊣ A provides a fork (5) called the 'canonical presentation' of a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use canonical presentation to relate an object a in A to the free/adjoint construction; example: for A = Grp, ea is the projection from the free group generated by underlying elements. Applying G to this fork gives a split fork in X which is the special case used in the comparison theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison of adjunctions (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'comparison' of F' to F is a functor M : A' -> A with M F' = F and G M = G'; such an M is a morphism of adjunctions and hence satisfies Me' = eM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons are the maps between categories arising from two adjunctions that induce the same monad; uniqueness/existence of such comparisons is central to proving that A ≅ X^T (or K an equivalence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of comparison when G creates coequalizers (lemma)
rubrics_metrics.description: If G satisfies the hypothesis (iii) of the theorem on the creation of coequalizers (i.e., G creates coequalizers), then there is a unique comparison M: A' -> A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof sketch: comparison must carry canonical presentations to canonical presentations; apply G to a fork and use that G creates coequalizers to get uniqueness. Use uniqueness to deduce isomorphism/equivalence of comparison functors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: G reflects colimits of T
rubrics_metrics.description: A functor G: A -> X reflects colimits of T: J -> A when every cone Je: T -> a for which GJe: GT -> Ga is a colimiting cone in X is already a colimiting cone in A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a general notion of 'reflects colimits of the diagram T'; special cases give reflecting coequalizers or reflecting isomorphisms. Use this to check whether colimit properties witnessed in X lift back to A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflects coequalizers (special case)
rubrics_metrics.description: G reflects coequalizers when every fork in A which becomes a coequalizer in X is already a coequalizer in A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A frequently used condition in variants of Beck's theorem; often easier to verify than creating coequalizers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflects isomorphisms (special case)
rubrics_metrics.description: G reflects isomorphisms when, for all arrows t of A, G t an isomorphism implies t an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This condition can replace reflecting all coequalizers in some hypotheses (see Exercise 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Weak Tripleability Theorem (Beck's thesis) — Exercise 2 (three-step criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) If A has all coequalizers, then K (comparison functor) has a left adjoint L. (b) If in addition G preserves all coequalizers, then the unit 1 -> KL is an isomorphism. (c) If in addition G reflects all coequalizers, then the counit LK -> 1 is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives stepwise conditions under which K admits a left adjoint and that the adjunction is an equivalence (unit/counit isomorphisms). Use as a checklist to prove monadicity/equivalence: existence of coequalizers in A, preservation by G, reflection by G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative hypothesis for Exercise 2 (Exercise 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A has all coequalizers, G preserves all coequalizers, and G reflects isomorphisms, then G reflects all coequalizers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a route to reflection-of-coequalizers via reflection-of-isomorphisms plus preservation; useful in verifying hypotheses of Exercise 2(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of comparison functor M via canonical presentations (construction detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: The comparison functor M : X^T -> A appears as a coequalizer diagram F G F x ==t F x -> M(x,h) (see Exercise 4(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows how to construct M explicitly as a coequalizer; useful when demonstrating existence of left adjoint or that K is essentially surjective/fully faithful.

rubrics_metrics.name: P — set of parallel pairs with split coequalizer and consequences (Exercise 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P be the set of parallel pairs f,g : a -> b in A such that Gf,Gg has a split coequalizer. Then: (a) If A has coequalizers of all pairs in P, K has a left adjoint M. (b) If G preserves all coequalizers of pairs in P, the unit 1 -> KM is an isomorphism. (c) If, in addition, G reflects coequalizers for all pairs in P, then the counit MK -> 1 is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A targeted variant: instead of requiring all coequalizers in A, restrict to those pairs whose images split in X; practical for dealing with forgetful functors where only some coequalizers are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence form of Beck's theorem (Exercise 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: For given adjunction data and comparison functor K, the following are equivalent: (i) K : A -> X^T is an equivalence. (ii) For any parallel pair f,g in A for which Gf,Gg has an absolute coequalizer, A has a coequalizer for f,g and G preserves and reflects coequalizers for these pairs. (iii) The same with 'absolute coequalizer' replaced by 'split coequalizer'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives necessary and sufficient conditions for K to be an equivalence (monadicity up to equivalence) in terms of coequalizers of those parallel pairs whose images have absolute/split coequalizers in X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of CG, SG, and the CTT/VTT/PTT properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Let CG be the set of parallel pairs <f,g> in A such that <Gf,Gg> has a coequalizer in X; let SG be the set such that <Gf,Gg> has a split coequalizer. Then: G has CTT when G has a left adjoint, preserves and reflects all coequalizers which exist, and A has coequalizers of all pairs in CG. G has VTT when G has a left adjoint, reflects coequalizers of all pairs in SG' and A has split coequalizers of all pairs in SG'. G is PTT when G has a left adjoint, preserves and reflects coequalizers for all pairs in SG' and when A has coequalizers of all pairs in SG'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These formal properties (Crude Tripleability Theorem = CTT, Vulgar Tripleability Theorem = VTT, Precise Tripleability Theorem = PTT) provide progressively weaker/stronger sufficient conditions for the comparison functor to be an equivalence. Note: CTT and VTT imply PTT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure properties: composition rules for CTT/VTT/PTT (Exercises 9-11)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Gj, G1, G3 are functors with Gj CTT, G1 PTT, and G3 VTT, then the composite G3 G1 Gj is PTT. The composite of two VTT functors is VTT. The composite of two CTT functors is CTT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when verifying monadicity for a composite forgetful functor by checking properties of intermediate forgetful steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety monadicity criterion (Theorem 1: <Q,E>-Alg -> Set)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let Q be a set of operators, E a set of identities, G the forgetful functor from (Q,E)-Alg to Set, and T the resulting monad in Set. Then the comparison functor K: (Q,E)-Alg -> Set^T is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof strategy: given a parallel pair whose underlying functions have an absolute coequalizer e: GA -> GB -> X in Set, define each n-ary operation on X uniquely by factoring through e^n (because e^n is a coequalizer), show identities lift, and prove the lifted map is a coequalizer in the algebra category. This gives that G creates the required coequalizers and hence monadicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for lifting algebra operations along an absolute coequalizer (proof detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: If e: B -> X is an absolute coequalizer in Set of underlying maps f,g in (Q,E)-Alg, then for each n-ary operator W in Q the map e^n is a coequalizer of f^n,g^n, so e W_B factors uniquely through e^n as W_X e^n, defining the W-action on X and making e a morphism of algebras.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the mechanism by which algebra structures are defined on the quotient set X; check closure of identities E to ensure X is a (Q,E)-algebra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monadicity of CmptHaus forgetful functor (Theorem: G : CmptHaus -> Set is monadic)
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard forgetful functor G from compact Hausdorff spaces to Set is monadic: G has a left adjoint (Stone-Čech compactification) and G creates coequalizers for suitable pairs arising from absolute coequalizers in Set by endowing the codomain with a unique compact Hausdorff topology making the quotient continuous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction uses the covariant power-set functor P to transfer the absolute coequalizer in Set to a coequalizer of closure operations: define the closure operation on W by factoring through P e, show e is continuous and closed, and verify compactness and Hausdorff property; then show e is a coequalizer in CmptHaus by universal property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict monoidal category axioms (associativity and unit equalities (1),(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A strict monoidal category <B, ⊗, e> is a category B with a bifunctor ⊗ : B x B -> B which is associative (⊗(⊗ x 1) = ⊗(1 x ⊗)) and with an object e which is a left and right unit for ⊗ (⊗(e x 1) = id_B = ⊗(1 x e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In strict case one identifies (B x B) x B with B x (B x B) and e ⊗ c = c = c ⊗ e strictly; interchange law for morphisms must also hold because ⊗ is a bifunctor. Many constructions (End(X), discrete monoids) are strict monoidal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relaxed (general) monoidal category axioms (alpha, lambda, rho and coherence diagrams)
rubrics_metrics.description: A (relaxed) monoidal category <B, ⊗, e, α, λ, ρ> has a bifunctor ⊗ associative up to a natural isomorphism α (the associator), left and right unit isomorphisms λ, ρ, and the pentagon and triangle coherence diagrams (equations (5) and (7)) must commute for all objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These coherence conditions guarantee that all reasonable parenthesizations / unit insertions are canonically isomorphic. When checking a structure is monoidal one must provide α, λ, ρ and verify the pentagon and triangle axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interchange law for a bifunctor
rubrics_metrics.description: For arrows f,f', g,g' with compositions defined, the bifunctor ⊗ satisfies the interchange law: (f ⊗ g) (f' ⊗ g') = (ff') ⊗ (gg').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required to ensure compatibility of ⊗ with morphism composition; must be checked when defining ⊗ on objects and arrows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence theorem and free monoidal category W (Theorem 1 of Coherence)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a monoidal category W (the free monoidal category on one generator) whose objects are binary words and for which, for any monoidal category B and any object b in B, there is a unique morphism of monoidal categories W -> B sending the generating blank to b. Consequence: every 'formal' diagram built from α, λ, ρ and ⊗ commutes in any monoidal category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use W to transport canonical equalities: define binary words, construct graphs Gn and G~ of basic arrows (instances of α, λ, ρ and identities), prove these graphs commute (via rank/induction and the pentagon/triangle axioms), and thereby deduce unique canonical maps between parenthesizations. Practical upshot: one need not verify ad hoc parenthesis/unit-isomorphism diagrams beyond the axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binary words and formal diagrams (definition used in coherence proof)
rubrics_metrics.description: Binary words are inductively defined: empty word eo, variable (-) of length 1, and if v,w are words of lengths m,n then v ⊗ w is a word of length m+n. For any two binary words v and w of the same length there is a designated arrow v -> w in W; these form the preorder category W used in the coherence proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This combinatorial setup underlies the construction of canonical maps and the argument that all formal diagrams commute; when checking coherence, phrase parenthesizations as binary words and compare via canonical maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical maps between word-functors (corollary)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any monoidal category B and any pair of words v,w of the same length n, there is a unique natural isomorphism can_B(v,w): v_B => w_B (the canonical map), satisfying that identities and the structural isomorphisms α, α^-1, λ, λ^-1, ρ, ρ^-1 are canonical and that composites and ⊗-products of canonical maps are canonical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This corollary encapsulates the coherence theorem in functional form: canonical maps provide the unique isomorphisms between any two parenthesizations/unit-insertions of an n-fold tensor; when constructing natural transformations between such functors, use the canonical maps.
